title: The Story of Islamic Imperialism in India
byline: by Sita Ram Goel · Voice of India · a 1982 series in the Organiser, later published as a book
lede: In 1982 the Indian Express reported guidelines from the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) for writing medieval history in school textbooks, framed around “national integration”. Goel answers them one by one. In his view the guidelines asked Hindus to forget a thousand years of conquest so that Muslims need not feel accused. He replies that national integration has to rest on truth, and that the truth is that Muslim rule in India was “an unmitigated evil”.

note: This is a polemic, and its verdict that Muslim rule had “no silver lining” is Goel's own. Most historians would describe the period's culture and politics in more mixed terms. This page lays out his rebuttals, attributed to him.

sections.title: Each guideline, and Goel's reply
head: NCERT guideline (as reported)
Goel's response
rows: Don't call ancient India the “Hindu period” or medieval India the “Muslim period”
Agreed, but then Muslim rulers must not be presented as natives either.
Don't rely on myths as history
Aimed at the epics. He says serious historians accept they hold a core of real history.
Aurangzeb is no longer the “champion of Islam”, and Shivaji is not to be “overglorified”
Aurangzeb's own chronicles praise his zeal. Every Hindu, not just Maharashtrians, honours Shivaji.
Don't describe the period as a Hindu–Muslim conflict
The Rajputs, Marathas, Sikhs and Jats were reclaiming their homeland from an alien empire.
Don't exaggerate religion's role in political conflict
The Muslim chroniclers themselves describe the wars as “mu'mins” against “kafirs”.
Don't call Muslims rulers and Hindus subjects, or the state a theocracy
Of the four schools of Islamic law, only the Hanafi allowed Hindus the alternative of jizya rather than “Islam or death”.
Stress assimilation, synthesis and a “composite culture”
He finds no synthesis in architecture, painting, music, science or philosophy, only Hindu skill put to Muslim use.

sections.title: Ruler by ruler
sections.lede: Goel works through the Muslim chroniclers' own accounts of each reign, from Mahmud to Aurangzeb. He includes Akbar, whom he calls a “myth” in chapter 10.
items: Goel argues Akbar's tolerance is overstated

sections.eyebrow: Chapter 8 · “the myth of Muslim empire in India”
sections.title: How much was ever ruled
items: From Sindh to Tarain, every advance was resisted (see Heroic Hindu Resistance).
Aibak's and Khalji's conquests did not hold.
Stable for about 150 years from 1556, and only with Rajput partners.

sections.eyebrow: Chapter 9 · the determinants of Hindu defeats
sections.title: Why Hindus lost, in Goel's view

items: Spiritual: a decline in Hindu thought from the 5th century
Cultural: the idea of one indivisible Bharatavarsha was forgotten
Mental: no alertness to the storm rising in Arabia, even as neighbours fell
A national rallying centre, as under Chandragupta and Skandagupta
Such centres came “too late”: Mewar under Pratap, Vijayanagara, Shivaji, Banda Bahadur
A forward policy to carry the war to the invaders' bases

sections.q: An average Muslim is as good or bad a human being as an average Hindu.
